title: Favorite trombone features and recordings that paid nothing
summary: Ridgley names Down Home Rag and Careless Love as pieces he liked, and says they recorded Hoy Nelli, Careless Love, Tuxedo Stomp and Black Rag but got no money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Did you have any licks on the trombone that used to bring a cheer from the crowd? Well, I don't know.
I played along pretty good and people thought I did pretty well.
I mean, would you have any pet ones that you really liked better than the others that would really bring the house down, a certain type of a trick that you would do?
I used to like down home rags. We recorded and called it Tuxedo Storm, down home rags. That was very good. Do you know that?
Yeah, I heard the record. Thank you.

That was my good. They had a trombone, a good trombone part there. And I used to like very much to play that. I used to make a little hit on it and I used to play a horn. Can I know that? I remember that. I was in the... I don't know. Cealous Love, you know I used to make... Cealous Love? Cealous Love, yes. Yeah, and make pretty good, and we recorded that too. But we got beat out those things. We didn't know nothing about it. We didn't get any money on it.
You mean you made up the tune and somebody else took it?
No, we recorded it. Oh, I see. We never did any money on it. We recorded a Hurinelli, Cealous Love, Tuxedo Stomp, and Black Rag. But we just didn't know we didn't get no money on it.
What kind of thought would you play it?
Otherwise our band went to pieces before we had a chance to get it to see, and I didn't take much interest in it.
What kind of thought would you play in that down room rag, you know? Hum it. I can't remember the thing.

That's it. So we went... You'd sing like that? Yes, sing. Really good. Sing on your trombone. Would you wiggle the slide, or what do you call that? Sometimes. Oh yeah, you do that. That action and all that was the infinite things that you played. Mm-hm. It was pretty good.
